trends.title: Over time
trends.heading: How your checks compare
trends.description: Each point is one visit, oldest on the left. This shows what the app heard — it is not a measure of how well or unwell you are.
trends.findingsChartTitle: Places the app flagged for a closer look
trends.findingsChartDescription: Out of the places recorded at each visit.
trends.confidenceChartDescription: Only shown for visits where the app named something. It is how sure the app was about its own guess, not a chance of illness.
trends.confidenceNone: The app did not name anything at any of these visits, so there is nothing to show here.
trends.qualityChartTitle: How many recordings were clear enough
trends.qualityChartDescription: A visit with few clear recordings tells you less than one with many.
trends.severityBody: Ausculta does not yet work out a severity score, so there is no severity line to draw. Nothing on this page is a severity score.
trends.changeDetected: A change in the recorded breathing sound pattern was noticed between your last two visits.
trends.noChangeDetected: No change in the recorded breathing sound pattern was noticed between your last two visits.
trends.changeNote: A change in the sound pattern is not the same as your health getting better or worse. Only a practitioner can tell you that.

empty.title: Not enough visits to show a trend yet
empty.body: A trend needs at least two visits to compare. Drawing a line through a single point would suggest a direction that nobody has measured.

rehab.title: Breathing plan
rehab.heading: Breathing exercises from your practitioner
rehab.whatItIs: Ausculta can carry a set of breathing exercises that a practitioner chooses for you. The exercises come from published clinical guidance, and only a practitioner can put them on your plan.

empty.title: Your practitioner has not given you a plan yet
empty.body: When a doctor or health practitioner assigns breathing exercises to you, they will appear on this page with instructions. Ausculta will not invent exercises for you — breathing exercises can be unsafe for the wrong person, so a practitioner has to choose them.
empty.body_example: When a doctor or health practitioner assigns breathing exercises, they appear on this page with instructions.

rehab.askNote: If you would like a breathing plan, ask your health worker or doctor at your next visit.
rehab.safetyBody: Read this before you need it. It explains the warning signs and what to do during an asthma attack.

shared.aboutTitle: What Ausculta can and cannot do
shared.aboutBody: Ausculta listens to recordings of your breathing and points out sounds a person may want to look at. It cannot diagnose an illness, it can be wrong, and it does not replace a doctor or a health worker. If you feel unwell, get help even if this app shows nothing.

noRecord.title: Your health record is not linked yet
noRecord.body: Your account is not yet connected to a patient record on this device. A health worker links them when they register you. Until then there is nothing of yours to show — this is not an error.
noRecord.action: What Ausculta can and cannot do

demoPreview.body: Your account has no patient record yet, so Ausculta is showing a made-up example so you can see how the app works. None of it is about you and none of it is real.
